epic.intent:
Add the person's new Onebrief role, **Manager, Outcome Engineering - Headless Agentic**, to the Experience page as the newest role on the existing Onebrief card in `src/data/jobs.ts`, with four sections for the core products they own and are architecting alongside their developers: **Onebrief Harness**, **Dark Factory**, **Onebrief Code Reviewer**, and **Evals and monitoring**.

**Who benefits:** recruiters, hiring managers and peers reading the portfolio, who see how the quality and agentic-testing work grew into a headless agentic outcome-engineering org.

**Out of scope:** metrics or achievement bullets the person has not supplied, changes to other employers or roles' content, layout or component changes, and any confidential Onebrief detail beyond what the person wrote.

successCriteria.text: The Onebrief card's first (newest) role is titled 'Onebrief - Manager, Outcome Engineering - Headless Agentic - <start date> - Present', and the 'Engineering Manager, Quality' role shows an end date instead of 'Present'.

The new role has four titled paragraphs, in order: 'Onebrief Harness', 'Dark Factory', 'Onebrief Code Reviewer', 'Evals and monitoring', each in the portfolio's first-person voice and faithful to the person's own description, with no invented metrics or claims.

Unit tests in src/data/jobs.test.ts assert the new role title, the four section titles in order, and key phrases from each; lint, format:check, test:unit, fireguard (no F), type-check, deadcode, build and test:e2e pass.

The change is merged to main via a PR with a posted red-team review, the Pages deploy succeeds, and the live Experience page shows the new role and its four sections at desktop width and at 375px with no horizontal scroll.

epic.title: Onebrief: Manager, Outcome Engineering - Headless Agentic role

bundle.rationale:
**Shape.** One sprint, since this is a small update: a role scaffold, then the four product sections as a strict chain (every ticket edits the same Onebrief role in `src/data/jobs.ts`, so parallel edits would conflict), then the ship ticket: PR, red-team review, CI, merge with the person's go-ahead, Pages deploy, live check. The person reviews dates and copy on the PR before giving the go-ahead to merge.

**Assumptions (change at a checkpoint if wrong):**
- Start date 11/01/2026, and the Engineering Manager, Quality role ends 11/01/2026. The person said they are starting the role but gave no date.
- The new role goes on the existing Onebrief card as roles[0], not as a new employer card.
- The four section titles are the product names exactly as the person gave them.
- No achievements list or metrics: the person supplied none, and the tickets must not invent any. Add bullets later when real outcomes exist.
- Copy stays faithful to the person's descriptions: grammar is tightened, nothing is added. 'Code rabbit' is written as CodeRabbit.
- No epic branch is named. Set one before the run (suggested: `epic/onebrief-outcome-engineering`).

**Process.** Each implementation ticket follows this repo's delivery standards: TDD first, the full gate, fireguard on new tests. The ship ticket carries the mandatory red-team review, and merging waits for the person.

exitCriteria.text: The person has confirmed the start date and the EM, Quality end date, and approved the copy of all four sections.
Every epic success criterion s1-s4 has recorded evidence, including the live page at desktop and 375px.

lint, format:check, test:unit, fireguard (no F), type-check, deadcode, build and test:e2e pass on the integrated changes.
